capabilities.title: Choose TransformerLens for GPT-style mechanistic interpretability
capabilities.summary: TransformerLens is the default for reading and editing decoder-transformer internals via HookPoints; other regimes call for a different tool.

when: reverse-engineering algorithms a GPT-style transformer learned during training
planning activation patching / causal tracing, attention-pattern study, circuit analysis, or direct logit attribution
needing HookPoints on every activation to read or modify model internals
avoid_when: working with non-transformer architectures (use nnsight or pyvene)
training or analyzing Sparse Autoencoders (use SAELens)
needing remote execution on massive models (use nnsight with NDIF)

steps: Confirm the target is a GPT-style / decoder transformer whose internals you need to read or edit via HookPoints on every activation; if so, use TransformerLens.
If the architecture is non-transformer, switch to nnsight or pyvene instead.
If the goal is training or analyzing Sparse Autoencoders, use SAELens instead.
If you need remote execution on massive models, use nnsight with NDIF instead.
If you want higher-level causal-intervention abstractions, use pyvene instead.

capabilities.title: Load a model as a HookedTransformer
capabilities.summary: Instantiate HookedTransformer.from_pretrained, supplying HF_TOKEN for gated models and choosing device/dtype, aware that weights are folded/centered by default.

when: needing a hooked wrapper around GPT-2 / LLaMA / Mistral / Pythia / GPT-Neo / OPT / Gemma / Phi models
avoid_when: the target architecture is not in the supported-models list

steps: Call HookedTransformer.from_pretrained("gpt2-small") or another OFFICIAL_MODEL_NAMES entry.
For gated models (e.g. meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf) set os.environ["HF_TOKEN"] before loading.
Pass device="cuda" and dtype=torch.float16 when you need to control placement or precision.

Note that from_pretrained folds LayerNorm and centers writing/unembed weights by default (fold_ln, center_writing_weights, center_unembed all True) — this changes weight semantics for downstream analysis.

validation: Print model.cfg.n_layers and model.cfg.n_heads to confirm the config loaded.
Confirm model.to_single_token(" Paris") returns an int without raising.
recovery: Gated-model download fails or 401 -> set os.environ["HF_TOKEN"] to a valid token before calling from_pretrained.

capabilities.title: Cache and read intermediate activations
capabilities.summary: Run the model with run_with_cache and index the ActivationCache by (key, layer) to inspect the residual stream, attention patterns, MLP outputs, and per-head q/k/v/z tensors.

when: needing intermediate activations (resid_pre/mid/post, attn_out, mlp_out, pattern, q/k/v, z) for any downstream analysis

steps: tokens = model.to_tokens(prompt); logits, cache = model.run_with_cache(tokens).
Index activations as cache[key, layer], e.g. cache["resid_post", 5], cache["pattern", 3], cache["z", layer].
To bound memory, pass names_filter=lambda n: "resid_post" in n (and/or "pattern") so only needed activations are cached.
For large models also pass device="cpu" to keep the cache off the GPU.

validation: Confirm len(cache.keys()) > 0 and that a sampled key matches its documented shape (e.g. cache["pattern", 0] is [batch, head, q_pos, k_pos]).
expected_outcomes: names_filter and device="cpu" reduce the cache's memory footprint
recovery: Out-of-memory on large models -> restrict with names_filter and/or set device="cpu" in run_with_cache.

capabilities.title: Activation patching (causal tracing)
capabilities.summary: Patch clean activations into a corrupted run across (layer, position) to localize which activations causally drive an output metric.

when: localizing which activations causally affect a specific model behavior or output
avoid_when: clean and corrupted prompts cannot be made to differ minimally, so the patching signal is uninterpretable

steps: Write clean and corrupted prompts that differ minimally (e.g. 'The Eiffel Tower is in the city of' vs 'The Colosseum is in the city of').
Define a metric capturing the behavior difference, e.g. logit_diff = logits[0,-1,paris] - logits[0,-1,rome] using model.to_single_token for the target ids.
Cache clean activations (_, clean_cache = model.run_with_cache(clean_tokens)) and record clean vs corrupted baseline metric values.

For each (layer, pos), define a hook that overwrites the activation with clean_cache[hook.name] at that position and call model.run_with_hooks(corrupted_tokens, fwd_hooks=[(f'blocks.{layer}.hook_resid_post', patch_hook)]).
Store the metric per (layer, pos) into a results tensor and visualize it as a layer x position heatmap to read off causal hotspots.

validation: The clean-baseline metric and corrupted-baseline metric differ (the prompt pair actually distinguishes the behavior).
Patching the identified hotspot moves the corrupted-run metric back toward the clean value.
recovery: Stale hooks from a previous run contaminate results -> call model.reset_hooks() before each run_with_hooks.
A metric target maps to multiple sub-tokens or the wrong id -> verify with model.to_str_tokens, use model.to_single_token, and check prepend_bos.

capabilities.title: Direct logit attribution / circuit analysis by head
capabilities.summary: Decompose a prediction's logit into per-attention-head contributions (z @ W_O @ W_U) to identify circuit components such as name-mover heads.

when: attributing a specific next-token prediction to individual attention heads
replicating circuits such as the IOI name-mover / backup-name-mover heads

steps: Set up the task with clear target tokens, e.g. IO vs S: john_token / mary_token via model.to_single_token.
Compute the baseline logit difference logits[0,-1,io] - logits[0,-1,s].
For each (layer, head) take the per-head output cache["z", layer][0,-1,head], project it through model.W_O[layer,head] and model.W_U (or dot with the target unembed direction model.W_U[:,target]).
Accumulate the contributions into an [n_layers, n_heads] tensor and rank the top heads with topk.
Validate the identified heads with ablation experiments.

validation: The baseline logit difference is computed and finite before decomposition.
Top head contributions align with the observed prediction direction; confirm by ablating the top heads.
recovery: Analysis ignores LayerNorm and yields wrong pre-activations -> apply the block's LayerNorm (e.g. model.blocks[layer].ln2) before projecting through weight matrices.
A head or target token maps to multiple sub-tokens -> check model.to_str_tokens and use model.to_single_token.

capabilities.title: Detect induction heads
capabilities.summary: Score each head by its attention from a repeated token back to the successor of its earlier occurrence to find [A][B]...[A]->[B] induction heads.

when: searching for induction heads that implement the [A][B]...[A]->[B] copy pattern

steps: Build a repeated token sequence (e.g. random tokens with the first half copied into the second half).
Run _, cache = model.run_with_cache(repeated_tokens).

For each layer read pattern = cache["pattern", layer][0] ([head, q_pos, k_pos]) and take the attention from the repeated position back to the earlier-occurrence successor position as the induction score.
Stack scores into an [n_layers, n_heads] tensor and take topk to list the strongest induction heads.

validation: The highest induction scores concentrate on a few heads rather than being uniform, and the topk list is non-empty and reproducible.
recovery: Sequence too short or not actually repeated -> ensure the second half exactly repeats the first so an induction target exists at the probed positions.
